title: Portable fixed-topology external time samples and deterministic interpolation

supportedProfile: Strict external JSON sample import into typed little-endian chunks with SHA-256
Nonuniform fixed-topology scalar/vector/position channels with explicit linear/step and outside policies
Native TeX local chunk hydration, immutable sampled attributes and downstream color visualization
excluded: Blender private bake cache interchange or execution of external solver code
Changing topology, adaptive time integration and general PDE correctness
Universal raster identity across devices or undocumented channel conversions

upstream.role: Conceptual comparison: structured metadata can identify selected binary ranges. Texloom defines an independent public manifest with fixed vertex topology, explicit time samples and exact payload SHA-256; it does not read Blender cache files.

license.note: Pinned source symbols inspected only for conceptual scope. No implementation is copied or translated. Any later source adaptation requires separate file-level license review.

inputs: Fixed mesh topology revision, exact ordered indices, units, finite strict sample times, seed and producer metadata
Declared scalar/vector/position channel kind and float32/float64 stored precision; frame-major channel-order LE bytes
Inline canonical base64 or explicit external URI/range with selected byteLength and SHA-256
outputs: A portable manifest, deterministic binary chunks and canonical emitted-manifest hash report
New immutable sampled mesh resources retaining raw scalar/vector attributes and optional sampled positions
Original native declarations, external manifest and selected binary payload archives with hashes and source spans
coordinates: Sample time is seconds; all vertex positions use explicit mesh units and no implicit conversion
Exact knots select one frame; intervals linearly blend decoded values or use the declared step policy
Interpolation keeps the exact topology snapshot, and field visualization reads sampled attributes rather than re-evaluating the producer formula
errorPolicy: Reject malformed JSON, duplicate keys, nonfinite data, float32 overflow, unknown fields and bounded input violations
Reject channel/count/topology/unit mismatch, missing chunks, invalid ranges and integrity failures before publication
Preserve existing importer output; native compile failures remove a stale published bundle
No previous-frame accumulation, silent topology correspondence, transport fallback or invented missing values

verification.command: python -m unittest tests.import_samples_test tests.sampled_field_capture_test tests.sampled_field_player_test tests.sampled_field_port_spec_test -v; npm test
claims: Mixed precision byte layout and canonical hashes are checked independently with Python struct/hashlib
Actual TeX imports seven nonuniform knots in four chunks and retains verified portable inline payloads
Original JSON independently supplies every expected scalar/vector/position at exact knots and cross-chunk intervals
Reverse PNG seeks, 30/60 fps histories, native GPU color interpolation and actual mobile controls are checked
Malformed paths, JSON, channel/topology references and corrupt bytes prevent publication
notEstablished: Accuracy of a PDE solver or the producer formula between time knots
Equivalence with Blender simulation zones or private cache encodings
Topology-changing interpolation or general scientific storage formats
Identical pixels across browsers and GPU drivers
